## Integrity (HARD RULES — non-negotiable)
- Close a `sorry` ONLY with a genuine proof. NEVER discharge it with a device that makes the file compile without actually proving the statement: no new `axiom`, no `admit`, no unproven auxiliary `axiom`/lemma cited by `exact`, no `decide` on a claim that is not genuinely decidable, no `@[implemented_by]`/`@[extern]` or `sorry` hidden inside a helper. - If a declaration is genuinely beyond you this turn, LEAVE its `sorry` exactly as it is (do not replace it with a fake discharge) and report honestly that you could not prove it, naming the decl and the concrete blocker (missing lemma, unclear step, integrability side-condition, etc.). - The only CausalSmith imports you may add or retain are same-run modules under `CausalSmith.Substrate.FiniteSideInformationMinimaxConvergence.*`. Paper/research modules and helpers from other runs are forbidden dependencies. If such a dependency is needed, leave the blocker and report it instead of copying the definition.

BUILD GREEN BEFORE YOU STOP. Do not return until you have built every Lean module you edited and

blocker. Run the actual targeted build (`lake build <edited modules>` from the `CausalSmith`
package) as your LAST step and read its output; do not trust a proof merely because it looks right
in the editor. A proof that does not compile is not done. If you report a genuine blocker, every
other edited module must still build cleanly.

diagnostics and exit status. For the LAST verification, capture the complete build output to a
temporary file while preserving the build status, then print an explicit `BUILD_EXIT=<status>` and

return only after the explicit preserved build status is `BUILD_EXIT=0`.
